Don Kissick

Libertarian candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Ohio · Open seat

U.S. Navy veteran; chair of the Libertarian Party of Ohio

Don Kissick is the Libertarian Party of Ohio's nominee for governor in 2026. His running mate for lieutenant governor is business owner James Mills. Kissick lives in Ottawa, Ohio, has chaired the Libertarian Party of Ohio since 2018, and ran before for U.S. Senate in 2024 and for U.S. House (OH-5) in 2018.

Where Kissick stands

Data centers
Calls for an immediate moratorium on all new data center construction, which he says a governor can impose by halting tax breaks. Says he would then work with lawmakers on rules for cooling, power use and impact on farmland.
Data centers (oversight)
Says he would appoint people to state boards who would fully scrutinize data center projects against environmental and construction standards.
License plate reader cameras (Flock)
Opposes automatic license plate recognition cameras, such as Flock cameras, and lists this as one of his three main issues.
Property taxes
Supports ending property taxes in Ohio.
Small business licensing
Supports simplifying licensing for small businesses.
Health care
Says he believes in medical freedom. Supports repealing laws that require health care providers to get government approval before they expand services.
Debates
Has asked to debate Vivek Ramaswamy and Amy Acton, either one or both, and has contacted the Ramaswamy campaign to set up a debate.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee for Governor of Ohio, 2026
  • Chair, Libertarian Party of Ohio Central Committee, 2018–present
  • Member, Libertarian Party of Ohio Central Committee (District 5), 2015–2017 and 2018–present
  • Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate, Ohio, 2024
  • Libertarian candidate for U.S. House, Ohio District 5, 2018
  • U.S. Navy, six years, including Desert Shield and Desert Storm deployments
  • Attended Ferris State University (technical communication), 1995–1998
  • Born in Royal Oak, Michigan; moved to Ohio in 2007; lives in Ottawa, Ohio
